citations.quote: When valuing assets and firms, we need to use discount rates that reflect the riskiness of the cash flows.
The expected returns on risky investments are then measured relative to the risk-free rate, with the risk creating an expected risk premium that is added to the risk-free rate.
If we consider all the financing that the firm takes on, the composite cost of financing will be a weighted average of the costs of equity and debt, and this weighted cost is the cost of capital.
To estimate the required rate of return on a share, analysts frequently use the capital asset pricing model (CAPM)

frontmatter_snapshot.summary: The discount rate is the return investors require to bear an asset's risk: a riskless rate plus a risk premium. CAPM operationalizes the premium as beta times the equity risk premium. Damodaran develops the foundation in Ch.4 and extends it through Ch.7 (riskless rate, ERP) and Ch.8 (cost-of-equity estimation).
frontmatter_snapshot.title: Discount Rate and Required Return Foundations
